A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FedStruct work. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and the algorithms, equations, experiments and displays can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original node-classification experiments on six datasets, including benchmark comparisons, pruning and representation ablations, and label-scarcity analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments on the six datasets and reports revised benchmark results, FedGCN comparisons and expanded robustness analyses.

M1.justification: The core decoupled predictor and Hop2Vec optimization remain. Pruning already existed, but its stated retention rule changes from the top p n_i entries of each intermediate matrix in v2 Appendix H.1 to ceil(p/K) n_i in v3 Appendix D.1. v3 also incorporates pruning into the default algorithm.

E1.justification: Both evaluate node classification on Cora, Citeseer, Pubmed, Chameleon, Amazon Photo and Amazon Ratings. The random, Louvain and K-means settings remain, as does the server-known global-graph scenario, moved from Appendix J to Appendix H. No new dataset or task coverage is established.

E2.justification: Table 2 replaces FedSage+ Ideal with FedGCN-2Hop. Table 6 removes the same idealized comparator and adds FedGCN-1Hop and FedGCN-2Hop. This materially changes the comparison against methods exploiting cross-client connections; the other principal baselines remain.

E3.justification: v3 uses pruning by default and extends the Chameleon client-count evaluation to 50 clients. The depth experiment sweeps GNN baseline depth instead of retaining v2's fixed three-layer controls. Main splits and listed training budgets remain. The exact depth-study client count is unclear: Figure 4(b) says five, while Section 6.2 says ten.

E4.justification: v3 adds a Cora visualization examining structural information retained after pruning and expands client-count robustness and depth analyses. Label-scarcity, pruning, structure-only inference and global-adjacency studies already existed. The original three-dataset feature-versus-structure comparison in Figure 1 is removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations over ten independent runs for Tables 2 and 6. No new seed disclosure, confidence intervals or formal significance-testing procedure appears. Changed standard-deviation values accompany revised results, without changing the reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 2 and 6 and the pruning comparison contain broadly revised scores. For example, Pubmed FedPub accuracy with ten randomly partitioned clients changes from 46.25±8.50 to 82.39±0.41. FedGCN and extended robustness results are added. These are reported result revisions, not established same-procedure improvements. v2 Table 9 and Figure 6 remain numerically unchanged as v3 Table 8 and Figure 6.

T1.justification: v3 adds the spectral polynomial-filter derivation in Section 5.2 and the FedGCN global-adjacency argument in Appendix C.4. Appendix D revises the matrix-block definitions and pruned acquisition equations, while Table 1 adds a client-count factor to the pruned communication bound. Most existing gradient proofs are retained and reorganized.

C1.justification: The FedStruct, Hop2Vec, feature-privacy, heterophily and near-centralized-performance claims remain. v3 adds an explicit near-FedGCN performance claim and presents the default pruned framework as jointly addressing privacy, communication and utility. The abstract's scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 substantially expands the mechanism discussion through spectral filtering, community preservation under pruning, and rank- and pruning-based arguments against adjacency reconstruction. It adds FedGCN privacy and implementation caveats and interprets the new comparisons. The earlier aggregate-sharing privacy mitigation and its unresolved approximate-reconstruction limitation remain.

D1.justification: The anonymous code address is replaced by a GitHub repository hyperlink. v3 newly specifies beta_Ls=1 and all other filter coefficients zero, but removes v2's statement about baseline defaults and learning-rate tuning. The p=30 hyperparameter row consolidates an existing disclosure; other listed hyperparameters and the Nvidia A30 hardware remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work is organized around known versus unknown cross-client connections, with added FedGCN discussion and citations to Chen et al. (2020) and Ngo et al. (2024). Li et al. (2018) and Fox and Rajamanickam (2019) are removed. The original explicit-structure and heterophily novelty positioning largely remains.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, method exposition and conclusion receive extensive rewriting. Label-scarcity and depth analyses move into the main evaluation, proofs are consolidated, and the appendices are reorganized. Terminology and notation are simplified throughout, beyond ordinary conference-header and numbering changes.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is replaced, framework Figures 2 and 5 are redrawn, and a pruning heatmap is added. Previously separate appendix plots are combined with other comparisons into the compact four-panel Figure 4. Tables gain revised organization, separators and ranking highlights; captions and overall layout change substantially.

improvement.justification: v3 adds a relevant FedGCN comparison, wider robustness sweeps and more explicit algorithm documentation. However, it introduces unresolved inconsistencies: Section 6 retains v2's Chameleon values 52.76/34.33 although Table 2 now reports 51.85/34.68; Figure 4(b) conflicts with Section 6.2 on client count; and Appendix D.2's worked matrices conflict with its starting graph. These reliability problems make the net benefit of the expanded evidence and explanations uncertain.
